> **What this case shows** — the [Kruskal-Wallis sibling](../gait-grf-pushoff-kruskal-gaitrec/index.qmd)
> found the vertical-GRF push-off peak separates the five gait classes; *which* pairs differ? Here **Dunn's
> test** — the non-parametric post-hoc — answers it under family-wise error control. The **newly-authored**
> `dunnTest` runs all 10 pairwise comparisons, reproducing **`PMCMRplus`** and **`scikit_posthocs`** to
> machine precision. Healthy controls differ from **all four** pathology classes, and — unlike the
> [dynamic range](../gait-grf-tukey-pathology-gaitrec/index.qmd) (Tukey: **0/6** pathology pairs) — the
> push-off peak **grades** the pathologies: **4/6** pathology-pathology pairs differ, with **calcaneus** the
> most distinct.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — the grouped feature → `dunnTest()` → read the pairwise comparisons.
**Way of thinking** — Dunn is to Kruskal-Wallis what Tukey is to ANOVA: the rank-based post-hoc for skewed
data. Running the same post-hoc on two GRF features and comparing the significance patterns shows which
feature does which job.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioMoCap::grfLandmarks()` (via the sibling), `PhysioAnalysis::dunnTest()`.
:::

## Proposition

In Dunn's post-hoc (Bonferroni) of the vertical-GRF push-off peak across GaitRec's five gait classes
(n=1844), all four healthy-vs-pathology pairs are significant (|z| up to 16.0) and 4 of the 6
pathology-pathology pairs are (calcaneus vs ankle/knee/hip, hip vs ankle); `dunnTest` reproduces
`PMCMRplus::kwAllPairsDunnTest` and `scikit_posthocs.posthoc_dunn` to machine precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is which classes differ, calibrated for multiplicity, on the feature that separates them.**
The Kruskal-Wallis sibling certified the omnibus difference and deferred the pairwise structure; this fold
performs the post-hoc, authoring the Dunn op and resolving the open question.

## Challenge & approach

We take the same certified per-subject push-off peak for the five classes and run `dunnTest` — all 10
pairwise rank comparisons with the shared tie-corrected variance and Bonferroni family-wise control —
checking every z-statistic against `PMCMRplus` and every adjusted p against `scikit_posthocs`.

```
GaitRec push-off peak, 5 classes (HC, A, K, H, C), n=1844 → dunnTest (Bonferroni, 10 comparisons)
  healthy vs pathology:   all 4 significant   (|z| up to 16.0)
  pathology vs pathology: C-A p~2e-6, C-K p~3e-13, C-H p~2e-15, H-A p~2e-3  (significant)
                          K-A p=0.067, H-K p=1.0                            (not significant)
     vs PMCMRplus::kwAllPairsDunnTest   → max |z|   ~ 2e-15
     vs scikit_posthocs.posthoc_dunn    → max |p|   ~ 7e-17
  contrast: dynamic range (Tukey) separated 0/6 pathology pairs; push-off separates 4/6
```

## Data

**GaitRec (Horsak et al. 2020)**: the vertical-GRF push-off peak for the five gait classes — healthy control
(n=208), ankle (n=483), knee (n=499), hip (n=364), calcaneus (n=290). The same matched cohort as the
Kruskal-Wallis sibling. Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the Dunn post-hoc −log10(adjusted p) matrix; a star marks significant pairs. Healthy control differs from every pathology class, and the calcaneus row/column lights up against the other pathologies. Right: the contrast — the dynamic range (Tukey) separated 0 of 6 pathology-pathology pairs, while the push-off peak (Dunn) separates 4 of 6. One feature flags impairment; the other grades it.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* on the left, a starred cell is a significant pairwise difference after family-wise
correction; the calcaneus group stands out from the other pathologies. On the right, the two GRF features
play complementary roles — the dynamic range is a healthy-vs-impaired switch, the push-off peak a
pathology gradient.

| Comparison group | result |
|---|---|
| healthy vs pathology (A, K, H, C) | **4/4 significant** (\|z\| up to 16.0) |
| pathology vs pathology (6 pairs) | **4/6 significant** (calcaneus vs A/K/H; hip vs ankle) |
| calcaneus vs ankle | p = 1.7e-6 (significant) |
| knee vs ankle / hip vs knee | p = 0.067 / 1.0 (not significant) |
| vs `PMCMRplus` (\|z diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~2e-15) |
| vs `scikit_posthocs` (\|p diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~7e-17) |

Every comparison equals both references to machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/dunn_summary.csv`](artifacts/dunn_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`dunnTest` reproduces the reference on the certified push-off peak. The transferable takeaway: **match the
post-hoc to the omnibus (Dunn after Kruskal-Wallis, as Tukey after ANOVA) and read the pattern across
features. Here two GRF landmarks divide the labour — the dynamic range separates healthy from pathological
gait, the push-off peak grades the pathologies, with the calcaneus (heel/ankle) group's propulsion deficit
the most distinct.**

## Open questions

- The push-off peak grades but does not fully separate the pathologies (knee-vs-ankle, hip-vs-knee remain
  non-significant); a multivariate GRF-landmark profile with a discriminant or classifier would give a
  fuller pathology fingerprint. The single-feature Dunn post-hoc is the honest answer for the push-off peak.
  *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| GRF landmarks (peaks, trough) | `grfLandmarks()` | PhysioMoCap |
| Kruskal-Wallis (omnibus) | `kruskalTest()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Dunn's test (rank post-hoc) | `dunnTest()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Tukey HSD (parametric post-hoc) | `tukeyHSD()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **adjusted p** — already corrected for all pairwise comparisons (Bonferroni); compare to your alpha
  directly.
- **the pattern across features** — running the post-hoc on more than one feature and comparing which pairs
  each separates is more informative than any single test.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

dunnTest(list(HC = hc_po, Ankle = a_po, Knee = k_po, Hip = h_po, Calcaneus = c_po), p_adjust = "bonferroni")
# a data frame of all pairwise z and family-wise-adjusted p -- machine precision vs PMCMRplus and scikit_posthocs
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/dunn_summary.csv`](artifacts/dunn_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
z-statistics and adjusted p-values, the machine-precision match against PMCMRplus and scikit_posthocs, the
healthy-vs-pathology (4/4) and pathology-pathology (4/6) significance split, the comparison count, and the
honestly noted scope (authors the new dunnTest op; push-off from the certified grfLandmarks; grades the
pathologies where the dynamic range did not; cross-sectional association).
